structuralFindings: ATR has multi-layer influence even though it is not a direct PriorityScore term: hard volatility gate -> stop geometry -> RR hard gate -> RR score/tie-break.
The ATR-to-stop mapping is channel-specific; B stop is directly volatility-scaled above the 1.2% floor while A may be pinned by support/structure and much less ATR-sensitive.
For B, low ATR values below the stop-floor crossover can produce identical stop/RR; above the crossover, higher ATR monotonically widens risk and reduces RR for fixed entry/target.
Therefore high-ATR B candidates can be rejected by RR<2 before reaching ranking even when atrPercent itself remains within the allowed <=10% gate.
The same ATR% does not imply the same effective penalty in A and B, so volatility calibration must be channel-conditional.
